tagline: A mountain road with a front-row seat on the Atomic Era.
intro: Deer Creek Road starts at Kyle Canyon Road, east of Mount Charleston, and heads north for 8.8 miles to Lee Canyon Road, first along the edge of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest and then into it. All of it, State Route 158, is a Nevada Scenic Byway.

Hilltop Campground sits high in the forest with a view over the valley and takes the occasional high wind for its trouble. About halfway along, at 8,300 feet, a seasonal stream runs beside the wooded path at the Deer Creek picnic area.

moments.title: Robber's Roost
moments.text: A short loop climbs a canyon to a couple of caves where, local folklore says, bandits hid goods and livestock taken from Mormon Trail travelers. Nobody knows if it is true.

moments.title: Mahogany Grove
moments.text: Beside the remains of a 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps campground, a short trail with signs tells the story of camping in the Spring Mountains.

moments.title: Desert View Overlook
moments.text: A paved path winds down to platforms looking out over the Mojave Desert, a vantage point in the Atomic Era for watching bomb detonations.

practical: The Desert View Overlook parking lot stays open in winter, but its trail is not cleared of snow.
